body.statement: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
body.justification: This remains the field-tier target because the new stress-tuple lower bound is not matched by a uniformly calibrated omnibus upper test and has not been optimized over all class parameters.
body.gap: The exact covariance-masking alternative invalidates the proposed pair-factor deterministic dichotomy; a richer population signal, sparse-occupancy concentration theorem, all-regime converse optimization, and equality-case analysis are required.
body.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and a total finite-sample procedure, without certifying a fitted forest or interpreting non-rejection as homogeneity.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a total multiresolution test whose population signal does not vanish on the exact covariance-masking alternative, prove uniform finite-sample level and power with every sparse-occupancy projection, and optimize it; independently extend and optimize the constant-null-supported direct-Hellinger converse over all \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), then compare the maps and determine every boundary logarithm.
obligation.obstruction: The lower route now closes at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), but it has not been optimized outside that tuple.  On the upper side, the explicit legal construction in \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) has \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) while \(g_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin.  Therefore both a canonical \(2+1\) kernel and a cross-fine \(2+2\) energy whose population means contain a within-bin pair factor have zero mean, so the required deterministic alternative dichotomy is false for that architecture.
obligation.attempted: The bounded-overlap margins were corrected and the class membership was rechecked.  Conditional on the macro signs, the exact common singleton likelihood was used as the dominating marginal.  The published partition-mixture lemma was instantiated with cell masses \(O(h)\), density ratios bounded by the original margins, \(\delta_1,\delta_2=O(\delta)\), and \(\delta_3=0\).  Convexity over the shared outer-sign prior left no extra outer term; the conditional cost \(n^2h\delta^2\) is absorbed at the mandated stress scaling, yielding the fixed-sample \(n^{-3/10}\) converse.  For the upper route, the binned covariance identity was solved exactly for a smooth baseline perturbation that cancels every proposed pair-factor population signal while retaining nonconstant CATE.
obligation.partial_result:
The unchanged-class all-regime bracket remains
\[
 c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n,
 \qquad
 b_n=\begin{cases}
 n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\leq4t,\\
 n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}.
\]
The no-penalty region \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\), \(d\leq4\gamma\), remains matched, with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  At the rough stress tuple \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the sign-conditioned common-marginal calculation proves the sharper original-class lower bound
\[
 c n^{-3/10}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad \rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{1/10}.
\]
The conditional partition-mixture calculation leaves \(n^2h\delta^2=O(\epsilon^7n^{-1/10})\), but this is absorbed by \(n^3hH\delta^4=\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\) for fixed \(\epsilon\) and large \(n\); no additional outer-sign term remains after Hellinger convexity.  The fixed-reference fifth projection remains a valid construction diagnostic but is not a Hellinger obstruction after normalization by the common singleton law.  On the upper side, an exact legal alternative with \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) and \(g_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin makes the proposed pair-factor \(2+1\) and \(2+2\) population means vanish.  A different omnibus population signal and its sparse-occupancy concentration theory are therefore still required, as are all-regime lower optimization, matching, and transition logarithms.  The frozen \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) remain diagnostics, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.
